summary:
Have you ever wondered how a flame burns in space? Conducting microgravity fire experiments in real life costs millions of dollars, making it impossible for most schools to access. That is why we created Flame in Freefall, an interactive 3D web application designed for students, educators, and space enthusiasts to explore the fascinating physics of combustion.   
flame-in-freefall-v6.html

In our 3D Virtual Lab, users can adjust gravity, oxygen levels, air pressure, and ventilation wind in real time. You can visually observe how a familiar yellow teardrop flame on Earth (1G) smoothly transforms into a spherical blue diffusion flame in microgravity (0G). Furthermore, the app integrates NASA’s FLEX and Saffire datasets with an AI Diagnostics Center. Users can trigger emergency scenarios, test spacecraft fire suppression protocols, and use AI Vision to analyze flame shapes. Flame in Freefall turns complex NASA science into an engaging, accessible learning experience for everyone.
details: 1. What does the project do and how does it work?Flame in Freefall is an interactive 3D Virtual Physics Lab and AI Fire Safety Diagnostics Center that runs directly in any web browser. It bridges the gap between Earth-based buoyant combustion (1G) and microgravity diffusion combustion (0G) through two core modules: flame-in-freefall-v6.html+ 13D Virtual Combustion Lab: Users can manipulate 5 environmental parameters in real time, Gravity (0G−1G0G−1G), Oxygen Concentration (10%−40%10%−40%), Atmospheric Pressure (0.2−3.0 atm0.2−3.0 atm), Ventilation Velocity (VventV vent​ from 0−2.0 m/s0−2.0 m/s), and Ambient Temperature (0−100∘C0−100 ∘ C), or switch between 4 NASA habitat presets (ISS, Moon, Mars, Earth). Our physics engine dynamically morphs the 3D flame from a yellow, upward-stretched teardrop at 1G (driven by Archimedes buoyancy) into a soot-free, spherical blue diffusion flame at 0G (where the Grashof number approaches zero). The flame obeys two NASA-derived extinction boundaries: it self-extinguishes when oxygen drops below the Limiting Oxygen Concentration (LOC) or when airflow exceeds the Blowoff Extinction Velocity (Damköhler number Da<1Da<1). Users can also trigger 4 emergency test cases and execute 3 spacecraft fire suppression protocols (N2N 2​ Inert Gas Injection, HVAC Shutoff, Bulkhead Isolation) while observing the flame's immediate response. flame-in-freefall-v6.html+ 3AI Diagnostics & NASA Data Explorer: Features a non-linear AI Hazard Index gauge that automatically triggers an audio-visual alarm and an automated 3-step suppression sequence if risk exceeds 85%85%. It integrates NASA Open APIs to query real microgravity combustion records (Saffire I–VI, FLEX-2, SoFIE, CIR), export datasets (.JSON/.CSV), sync real Cygnus/ISS experimental telemetry directly into the 3D Lab, and analyze flame imagery using Google Gemini Vision AI (with a built-in Offline NASA Engine fallback). flame-in-freefall-v6.html+ 12. What are the benefits and expected impact?Democratizing Million-Dollar Space Experiments: Real microgravity combustion experiments require drop towers, parabolic flights, or ISS orbital racks costing millions of dollars. Flame in Freefall puts a virtual ISS combustion rack into the hands of students, teachers, and the public for free on any smartphone or PC. flame-in-freefall-v6.htmlVisualizing Counter-Intuitive Physics: Transforms abstract concepts, such as thermal buoyancy, molecular diffusion, radiative heat loss, soot formation, and invisible "Cool Flames", into tangible visual experiences via 3 optical modes (0G Blue Diffusion, FLIR Thermal IR, and Vector Streamlines). flame-in-freefall-v6.htmlSpacecraft Fire Safety Awareness: Educates future engineers and students on why gentle HVAC ventilation in microgravity actually accelerates fire spread rather than cooling it, preparing learners for next-generation lunar and Martian habitats (Exploration Atmospheres with low pressure and enriched oxygen). flame-in-freefall-v6.html3. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?Core Languages: HTML5, CSS3 (Glassmorphism UI, responsive grid, CSS matrix zoom transitions), and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+) architected as a zero-dependency, single-file web application. flame-in-freefall-v6.html3D Graphics & Shaders: Three.js (WebGL r128), OrbitControls, and custom GLSL Vertex & Fragment Shaders for real-time procedural geometry deformation and spectral color rendering. flame-in-freefall-v6.htmlAI & Space APIs: Google Gemini Multimodal API (with dynamic model discovery), NASA Open API (api.nasa.gov/techport), NASA Glenn Media Archive API, and curated telemetry from NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI). flame-in-freefall-v6.htmlWeb Hardware & Audio APIs: Web Audio API (AudioContext, OscillatorNode) for procedural ambient chords and dual-tone emergency sirens (960 Hz/720 Hz960 Hz/720 Hz); WebRTC getUserMedia for live camera scanning; and the Vibration API for mobile haptic feedback. flame-in-freefall-v6.html4. How is your project creative?Procedural GLSL Flame Morphing: Instead of relying on pre-rendered videos or static 3D meshes, we mathematically deform a sphere in the vertex shader, interpolating between spherical diffusion and buoyant teardrop equations while applying multi-frequency harmonic turbulence. flame-in-freefall-v6.htmlNon-Linear Damköhler Hazard Modeling: Our risk algorithm models the real bell-shaped effect of microgravity airflow (low-to-moderate ventilation feeds fresh O2O 2​ and spikes hazard, whereas high velocity stretches the reaction zone and blows the flame out) alongside exponential oxygen enrichment. flame-in-freefall-v6.htmlClosed-Loop NASA Data-to-Lab-to-AI Pipeline: Users can search NASA’s Saffire/FLEX records, inject those exact experimental parameters into the 3D Lab with one click, capture the resulting 3D WebGL frame into the AI scanner, and generate comparative physical diagnostics. flame-in-freefall-v6.htmlProcedural Crew Dragon & Solar System Lobby: The lobby background features a fully procedural 3D SpaceX Crew Dragon spacecraft flying on a closed Catmull-Rom spline through the Solar System with 1,500 instanced asteroids. flame-in-freefall-v6.html5. What factors did your team consider?Scientific Rigor vs. Educational Simplicity: We carefully translated complex combustion metrics (Grashof number, Damköhler blowoff, LOC thresholds) into intuitive sliders and visual feedback suitable for K-12 and university students. flame-in-freefall-v6.htmlCross-Device Performance Optimization: We implemented an adaptive particle governor that monitors real-time FPS and scales particle draw ranges on low-end mobile devices, while pausing background WebGL contexts when switching tabs. flame-in-freefall-v6.htmlAccessibility & Safety: Full support for prefers-reduced-motion (disabling auto-rotation and heavy animations) and clear disclaimers distinguishing educational simulation from certified flight hardware. flame-in-freefall-v6.htmlFrictionless Judge & User Experience: By building a deterministic Offline NASA Physics Engine alongside Cloud Gemini AI, we ensured that judges and students without an API key can still test every single feature seamlessly. flame-in-freefall-v6.html
